nächst.et: See nächster. Compare the Dutch preposition naast (“next to”).

nächster.et: From Old High German nāhisto, from Proto-Germanic *nēhwist (“nearest, closest”). Compare Dutch naast, English next, Danish næste, Swedish nästa.

Nächstenliebe.et: From nächsten + Liebe. Compare Dutch naastenliefde.

s: to repeat something said by someone else; to echo; to follow someone's opinion
to say (something about someone, often something negative); to spread rumours about someone.

to (have a) look; to look and see, to check

Nachschub.et: 15th century construction from nach + Schub. Synchronically analyzable as deverbal from nachschieben.

s: to place after, to make postpositive
to hunt, to follow, to stalk, to pursue, to go after
to check, to look into, to investigate, to explore, to consider

to look up (obtain information about something from a text source)
to look at (something) as it moves away
Sehnsüchtig sah er dem Zug nach, bis er am Horizont verschwand.

to forgive, excuse, be understanding about
postlude, epilogue (final part of a piece)
das wird ein politisches Nachspiel haben

Nachspielzeit.et: Analysable as nach (“after”) + Spiel (“game”) + Zeit (“time”) or as nachspielen (“to re-play, to make up for missed play”) + Zeit (“time”).

s: Je mehr ich darüber nachsann, desto klarer wurde es, dass wir alle einem Betrüger aufgesessen waren.
to jump in after (someone), to follow (someone) while jumping
er sprang dem Kind ins Wasser nach

to run after, to chase after
to add (i.e. to a message, statement, question)
to enjoy one’s freedom in religious or (by extension) other matters of life; used in contexts advocating tolerance
nach seiner Fasson selig werden.et: Literally, “to go to heaven in one’s own fashion”. After a note that Frederick the Great wrote on a memorandum concerning the role of the Catholic Church, suggesting that every Prussian subject should be able to do so.

不过确实有一个好处，即使是这种先验研究最笨、最不情愿的学徒，也能理解它、也会在意它，那就是：只忙于经验使用、从不反思自己知识来源的知性，虽然可以过得很好，却有一件事完全做不到，即为自己规定使用的界限，知道什么在它的整个领域之内、什么在其外；因为这恰恰需要我们所做的那些深入研究。
